unit.why: Narrative of R. Shmelke's arrival at Nikolsburg as rabbi, his private self-greeting overheard by hidden townsmen, and his explanation of it as a guard against pride.

stories.start_quote: ויהי שמות האחים הצדיקים הלוך וגדול
stories.summary_en: On arriving as rabbi of Nikolsburg, R. Shmelke asks for two hours alone, during which hidden townsmen hear him greet himself sighing 'Peace to you, rabbi of Nikolsburg'; asked why, he explains via 'let your fellow's honor be dear to you as your own' that he did so to inure himself against the pride their honors might bring.
